newsitem.title: USA: Ventritex CEO sees improved results in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Ventritex CEO sees improved results in Q1.

text.p: Ventritex Inc's chief executive officer said the medical device maker's sales and net operating results this quarter should significantly improve from the previous, or fourth quarter results.
Ventritex lost $0.52 a share in the fourth quarter ended June 30 on sales of $17.3 million.

CEO Frank Fisher, in an interview following a presentation at the Montgomery Securities Investment Conference, also said he expects the company will break even in the March 1997 quarter, its third fiscal quarter.
Ventritex in September received U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval to market its new Contour implantable defibrillator and sales of that product should boost revenues.
Ventritex has been losing money since the fiscal 1995 fourth quarter due to a change in U.S. regulations on medical device approval, he added.
